prompts.kilnfoldPrompt: Create ONE 2x2 illustration atlas: four equal square panels in a square image, separated by generous warm ivory paper gaps WITHOUT lines, borders, text or labels. Every panel is an independently composed candid scene, NOT a lineup or portrait. A distinct principal adult person clearly dominates each scene; any secondary people are understated. Faces ordinary and imperfect, lean working bodies, natural adult head/body/leg proportions, no glamorous advertising expressions, heroic posing or theatrical rags. Full gestures fit within each panel. First 300 years of a fictional human civilization with handmade early tools. Graphic matte gouache, flat broad ochre/charcoal/umber/sage pigment, dry brush grain, broken edges fading into ivory. No photography, glossy realism, fantasy, recognizable historical national costumes, modern objects or writing. Invention must come from credible materials and distinct social activities. One coherent invented population: deep brown skin, coarse loosely coiled dark hair, varied faces with subtly broad cheekbones and long noses. Shared cultural dress uses smoke-gray sleeveless overwraps folded SIDEWAYS under one arm, brick-ochre waist ties, small unglazed clay clasps. Panel top left: older narrow-faced woman with cropped graying hair squats beside a drying clay wall, tracing a crack with one finger while speaking up to someone beyond the frame. Top right: lanky balding man with large ears stands SIDE ON, demonstrating a clay vessel's cracked base with both hands, irritated concentration. Bottom left: young adult woman with tied coarse curls lifts the corner of a woven cover over drying clay tablets with no writing, checking them while leaning forward. Bottom right: wiry middle-aged man with uneven beard seated cross-legged on a low reed mat, one hand around a small cup, the other making a restrained gesture during negotiation. Composition and poses all different.

prompts.civicScenePrompt: Create ONE square 2x2 atlas of four CLEARLY DIFFERENT early civilization civic scenes. Equal square panels separated by broad ivory paper gaps, no border lines, words or labels. Strict aesthetic: spare flat matte gouache, CHARCOAL HUMAN SILHOUETTES WITH MINIMAL FACE MARKS, broad ochre/umber/sage pigment shapes, visible dry grain on warm ivory fibrous paper. Not photographic, not realistic painted faces, not cinematic. Ordinary natural adult anatomy, practical invented early woven clothing, handmade wood/stone/reed tools. Each panel's image fades into paper, sparse scene not densely rendered. Top left COMMAND: a standing leader interrupts with a firm downward hand gesture above a low planning surface, two spear-bearing guards behind at a distance and two listeners lower in frame; clipped body language, authority and tension, NO violence or cartoon villain expression. Top right COUNCIL: four adults sit at equal height in a loose asymmetric circle, one speaks with a raised open hand while another turns toward a disagreeing participant; no central throne or heroic figure, actual disagreement and listening. Bottom left STEWARDSHIP: two adults crouch beside a leaking small clay water channel, one touches a crack and the other lifts a reed mat, a third brings a plain repair basket; hands-on care for shared infrastructure, no smiling advertisement. Bottom right EXCHANGE: two adults stand facing obliquely across baskets and tools, one offers a measure while the other counts a few pebbles, distant carrying figure. Peoples remain anonymous graphic silhouettes so the scene represents civic practice rather than dictating ancestry. Do not repeat characters, gestures, poses or layouts across panels. No copies of a portrait cast.
